meta.note: Supply only. 2026 = harvest to date plus the rest of the year at the same pace; 2027 = our harvest projection times the 6 kg+ share expected, low and high cases in brackets.

basins.name: Norway
basins.how: 6 kg+ harvested month by month from the biomass register (every farm, gutted weight, our size model): 247 kt in 2025, 240 kt from January to September 2026, plus October–December from the generations model. 2027: the model gives January–September 2027 against the same months of 2026: +20 % central, +2 % if the new generation loses its growth advance, +30 % if it keeps all of it; October–December 2027 carried at the same rate. Cross-check: the size split of the Sitagri price index (fresh whole salmon traded on the spot market by the exporters that report to the index, not the whole harvest) shows 6 kg+ at 11.9 % of the volume in 2025 and 15.7 % so far in 2026, the same direction.
known: H1 2026: 166 kt of 6 kg+ against 120 kt in H1 2025 (+39 %).
Fish over 5 kg at sea at the end of September: 52 kt gutted against 39 kt a year earlier (+34 %).
The generation being harvested grows 14 % faster per fish and loses 0.85 % of its fish a month (1.43 % a year earlier).
Next generation: 283 M fish at 1.07 kg (289 M at 1.00 kg a year earlier).
October 2026: 14.5 % of the harvest in 6 kg+ (13.1 % a year earlier), from harvest-boat visits.
up: Stock already in the water: 52 kt of fish over 5 kg at the end of September (+34 %), and they keep growing through the winter: most of the 6 kg+ of H1 2027 are these fish.

The next generation is ahead: 1.07 kg per fish against 1.00 kg a year earlier, growing faster. If it keeps the advance, it reaches 6 kg in spring–summer 2027 and the usual April–July gap in big fish disappears (+30 % case).
Fewer losses: the generation being harvested loses 0.85 % of its fish a month against 1.43 % a year earlier, so more fish reach large sizes.
Farmers can keep fish longer when lice and disease leave them alone: fewer forced harvests of small fish.
down: The growth advance fades: if the new generation grows like an average one, 6 kg+ are only +2 % in January–September 2027.
Biology goes back to normal (see the box): more lice, more delousing, more handling deaths, more early harvests.
Algae (spring 2026 in the south, 2025 in the north), ISA, pasteurellosis or a jellyfish year force early harvests of smaller fish.
Weak premium for big sizes: farmers may prefer to harvest earlier and free biomass for the next generation.
Norway is at its legal biomass limit (MTB): more 6 kg+ means fewer small fish, not more salmon; if farmers near their limit, they harvest earlier.

biology.title: Biology in 2026: the best year in a long time — and a limit for 2027
lines: Mortality at sea, January–Sep: 6.8 % of the fish (30 M fish) against 8.5 % (40 M) in 2025 and 8.5–9.6 % in 2019–2025: the lowest since at least 2019.
Sea lice, weeks 1–44: 0.134 adult females per fish on average against 0.175 in 2025 (0.134–0.175 since 2019).
Farm-weeks above the lice limit: 360 against 893 in 2025 (467–959 since 2019).
Non-medicinal delousing (thermal, mechanical, freshwater) reported: 2,613 against 3,263 in 2025 (-20 %): fewer handlings, fewer injuries.
Sea at the farms 9.4 °C on average against 9.8 °C in 2025: the cool summer slowed lice; the fish still grew faster than a year earlier.
limits: A year this good is rarely repeated: low mortality and few treatments in 2026 left more and bigger fish at sea, which is why the 2027 projection is high. If 2027 is an ordinary year, part of that advance is lost.
Temperature: a warmer 2027 (like 2025, 9.8 °C) brings lice back, then delousing and handling deaths, and earlier harvests of smaller fish.
After low-lice years, pressure tends to come back: 2023 was as calm as 2026 for lice, and 2024 was one of the worst.
More big fish at sea also means more biomass to manage under the MTB limit: farmers close to their limit harvest earlier, which caps the 6 kg+.
The algae episode of March 2026 in the south (about 1.7 million fish in zone 1) shows the risk is still there, even in a good year.
biology.source: Biomass register (Fiskeridirektoratet), monthly; BarentsWatch weekly lice and treatment reports by farm.

basins.name: Chile
basins.how: Atlantic harvest (724 kt in 2025, 740 kt in 2026) × share of 6 kg+ estimated from the average harvest weight reported by Camanchaca and Multi X (5.17 kg live in 2025, 5.02 kg in 2026Q1; estimated share 20 % and 16 %, assuming the usual spread of weights). Customs confirm the direction: 6 kg+ were 35 % of the whole Atlantic salmon exported over the last six months against 42 % a year earlier. 2027: harvest -2.1 % at the 2026 weight; low case: harvest -9 % and 0.3 kg lighter fish; high case: harvest +1 % and back to 2025 weights.
known: Standing biomass about 7 % below a year earlier; harvest slowing since August.
Record El Niño: Chilean sea 1–3 °C above normal; preventive algae emergency from 1 Nov 2026 to 30 Jun 2027.
Sea lice at a high (65 farms above the threshold in Q3 2026); SRS causes 53 % of infectious mortality (2025) and forced early harvests at Camanchaca in Q1 2026.
FOB price of 6 kg+ up 16 % in Q3 2026 as volumes fell.
up: A mild algae season and calmer El Niño let farmers grow fish to full size.
Fewer early harvests for lice and SRS.
down: A bloom like 2016 or 2021 in the inner seas (Los Lagos, Aysén) or new losses in Magallanes.
Warm water speeds growth but pushes farmers to harvest early, at smaller sizes, to limit risk.
Companies changing hands (Blumar sold to Agrosuper) may change harvest plans.

question.q: Could H1 2027 look like H1 2026 in Chile?
lines: H1 2026 was strong: Atlantic harvest +16.5 % on a year earlier in January–April and +7.9 % in January–June (Subpesca).

Big fish were plentiful early in 2026: 6 kg+ were 36 % of whole exports in Jan (35 % a year earlier), 39 % of whole exports in Feb (27 % a year earlier), 31 % of whole exports in Mar (26 % a year earlier).
That came from a record stock at sea in 2025: biomass +12 to +21 % above 2024 month by month (Sernapesca).

Most fish harvested in H1 2027 went to sea between mid-2025 and early 2026. The pipeline behind them is not bigger: fish in freshwater farms (all salmonids, future smolts) were −4 %, −3 %, −7 % in October–December 2025 against a year earlier (Sernapesca).
The harvest has already turned down: Aug −6 %, Sep −2 % on a year earlier.

Health and climate weigh on H1 2027: preventive algae emergency to June 2027 under a record El Niño, sea lice at a high, SRS behind 53 % of infectious deaths; all push farmers to harvest earlier and smaller.
question.verdict: Unlikely: H1 2027 should bring a flat or lower harvest and fewer 6 kg+ than H1 2026. It would take a mild algae season and fewer early harvests to get close.
question.caveat: Chile publishes no current stock at sea: Sernapesca's monthly biomass comes once a year (2025 figures published in March 2026). Subpesca's stocking resolutions give the number of fish allowed per farm, not the number actually stocked, so they are not used here.

basins.name: Faroe Islands
basins.how: Harvest (115 kt in 2025, 136 kt in 2026) × share of 6 kg+ estimated from Bakkafrost's average harvest weight (gutted): 5.7 kg in H1 2026 against 5.1 kg in H1 2025, back to 5.0 kg in Q3 2026 (estimated share 39 % in 2025, 46 % in 2026, assuming the usual spread of weights). 2027: flat harvest (Bakkafrost plans as much as in 2026) with more even harvests through the year: fewer big fish than in H1 2026 and slightly fewer over the year, but still mostly large fish, aimed at the United States and China; we take 5.4 kg on average (low case 5.1 kg, high case 5.6 kg).
known: H1 2026 was a big-fish half-year: 5.7 kg on average against 5.1 kg a year earlier (about 27 kt of 6 kg+ at Bakkafrost against 11 kt, estimated); Q3 2026 back to 5.0 kg.
Where Faroese whole salmon goes in 2026: United States 19 %, China 15 % of the tonnes (Faroese export statistics).

Bakkafrost Faroes harvest guidance 2026: 97,000 t (raised from 92,000 t in May); smolts put to sea in 2026: 9.5 million in H1, 4.5 million in Q3; average smolt weight 527 g in Q1 2026 (449 g in 2025).
SEB on Q2 2026: heavier fish (5.6 kg vs 5.0 kg) but the premium for larger fish remained limited.
up: Strategy: keep most of the harvest large for the United States and China (Faroese salmon has entered the US duty-free since August 2026, against about 12 % for Norway and Chile).
Larger smolts (527 g in Q1 2026) and good biology.
down: More even harvests through 2027: fewer 6 kg+ in the first half than in H1 2026.
The fish harvested since July 2026 are lighter (5.0 kg); a weak premium for big sizes makes earlier harvests tempting.

basins.name: Iceland
known: Fish over 5 kg at sea in 2026-09: 6.4 kt against 10.6 kt a year earlier (-40 %); 4–5 kg: 7.4 kt against 9.2 kt (MAST).

basins.name: Scotland
known: Scottish farmers harvested early in 2026 because of gill disease and mortality (Scottish Sea Farms cut its 2026 harvest guidance by 3,000 t; Bakkafrost Scotland ended external smolt sourcing after biological setbacks). Bakkafrost Scotland harvest weight: 6.4 kg in Q1 2026, 5.2 kg in Q2 (4.4 kg in June). No national size statistics.

lead: 6 kg+ salmon from Norway, Chile and the Faroes: about 506 kt in 2026 (+15 % on 2025) and 567 kt in 2027 (+12 %, range 433–644 kt). Norway drives the change; more big fish in Norway; fewer in Faroe Islands, Iceland, Scotland.
